title: Inside Harbinger's $300 Million EV Deal
summary:
Harbinger Motors just landed a huge deal: 2,000 all‑electric trucks headed to FedEx in a contract worth over $300 million.
Harbinger Motors CEO John Harris joins Bloomberg Open Interest to tell us how the EV maker plans to scale up, what soaring fuel prices mean for big fleets, and why demand is surging even without new green regulations. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NYSE Is Making Improvements, Other Are Not, Martin Says

title: ECB Wary of Stepping Into French Bond Turmoil
summary:
A sudden selloff of French bonds has stirred memories of the sovereign debt crisis that cascaded across Europe between 2009 and 2015. Attention is now turning to how the European Central Bank might respond. 
Virginie Maisonneuve, founder at Maisonneuve Global Advisors, discusses the global economic outlook and why the ECB is wary of the current French bond turmoil. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: PepsiCo Lowers Guidance; Levi Strauss Sales Growth Disappoints | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- PepsiCo (PEP) shares are lower after the company decreased its profit outlook, with its recovery in North America taking longer than expected. PepsiCo faces higher costs in North America that are weighing on margins, and will be raising some prices in the coming months after cutting prices on some marquee brands earlier this year.
- Microsoft (MSFT) shares are following news the company's Xbox unit is formalizing its film and TV foray with a new division called XP to expand its franchises into other media.
- Levi Strauss (LEVI) is lower after it posted the slowest growth in its direct-to-consumer channels since late 2022, in part due to a marketing misstep. The company expects direct-to-consumer growth for the current quarter to increase by a mid-single digit, after changing its marketing to focus on low-rise jeans. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Startups Rival Private Equity for Talent
summary: Private equity is still winning Wall Street's talent war, but the battlefield is shifting. As buyout firms aggressively poach junior bankers, AI startups dangle equity upside and supercharged growth. With AI tools reshaping entry-level roles and payouts at the top swelling again, finance is racing to prove it can still offer the best long-term bet for ambitious young talent. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Maduro Faces New Charge Over Torture of US Citizens in Venezuela
summary: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife face a new criminal charge that they are responsible for the torture of US citizens detained in the South American country.

title: JetBio to Add Ethanol-to-Diesel Capacity at Proposed Plant
summary: JetBio has redesigned a planned $2 billion sustainable aviation fuel plant to also manufacture diesel from ethanol because of slower-than-expected growth in green jet fuel demand.

title: J&J CEO Joaquin Duato on Obesity, Cancer and AI | The David Rubenstein Show
summary: Johnson & Johnson CEO Joaquin Duato says the company has no plans to enter the obesity market, instead focusing on areas such as cancer. He says oncology remains one of J&J's core growth pillars, and highlights dementia as another major challenge for the healthcare industry. Duato also talked about how artificial intelligence could accelerate drug discovery and the development of new medicines. He's on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded June 16 at The Economic Club of Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bank of Ireland’s Soured Deals Show Hazard in SRT Boom
summary: Investors have written down two risk transfer deals with Bank of Ireland Group Plc as the underlying loans deteriorate, a warning of the potential pitfalls involved in the increasingly popular trades.

title: BOE's Bailey Says Fiscal Policy Risks Becoming Less Effective
summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that governments may be left helpless in the event of another downturn as their firepower is sapped by weak growth and a series of severe shocks. "Fiscal policy can operate as a countercyclical tool of policy," Bailey said at an event in Turkey. "But if the negative shocks come at higher frequency, and underlying growth in the economy is lower, countercyclical policy becomes very difficult to follow successfully." (Source: TCMB Istanbul Economic Forum)

title: Windshield Repair Group Belron Picks Banks for Europe IPO
